newsitem.title: USA: HSN sees electronic commerce growing.
newsitem.headline: HSN sees electronic commerce growing.

text.p: Barry Diller, chairman of HSN Inc, parent of the Home Shopping Network, said Tuesday that he expects electronic commerce to grow into a large business in the next several years.

"The wind is at the back of electronic commerce," Diller said during a telephone conference call with analysts and reporters. "In the next several years, the ability to offer it to others, we believe, is a truly large business."

Earlier, HSN announced it planned to acquire a 47.5 percent stake in Ticketmaster Group Inc from chairman and major stockholder Paul Allen, the co-founder of Microsoft Corp, in a stock-for-stock transaction.

Diller said that he saw "cross interest possibilities" between HSN's Home Shopping unit and its Silver King Broadcasting unit, which owns 12 UHF TV stations, especially in expanding and offering its core transactional processing business for others to sell their goods and services.
"There are really good cross interest possibilities," Diller said Diller. "All of that is in the future."
Fred Rosen, chief executive of Ticketmaster, said during the conference call the two companies's "talents and skills are complementary."

"We're interested in the size and scope of what can be done in the transactional business," Rosen said. "The whole world of electronic transactions and convenience for consumers is only going to get larger."
In answer to an analyst's question, Rosen said Ticketmaster's processing capacity "is far from being used. We don't have warehouse capacity. This gives us a leg up..."

On the conference call, money manager Mario Gabelli criticized both Ticketmaster and HSN for not offering Ticketmaster shareholders a premium. "This deal stinks," said Gabelli. "How do you justify it for the shareholders of Ticketmaster? It's missing the guts of corporate responsibility."
Gabelli, who owns shares of HSN, was not immediately available for further comment.
Officials from both HSN and Ticketmaster defended the deal. "All of us are interested in creating value for shareholders," Rosen said.
"It's an extremely positive development. Over a period of time, it will add more value and more strength to this company," he said.
